_purpose: Phase 5C + 5D. Frozen protocol for joint (Delta, Gamma, Vega) estimation and the economics of transform reuse. Written after the Phase-5B results (which chose the scheduler below on a different grid) and committed before this study is run.

scheduler.choice_reason: Phase 5B (results/phase5_sampling_policy/study): digital shifts were feasible in every tested cell, met the deadline criterion, kept 95% coverage, and had 0.09x the time-normalised MSE of Owen scrambling. The 'ci' objective was a further 0.57x but uses 4-5 replicates, too few to estimate a 3x3 error covariance; the vector study therefore keeps r_min = 8.
scheduler.mc_blocks: MC blocks are capped at asian_qmc.mc_block(m) paths (about 2^15 normals). Phase 5B showed the uncapped look-ahead MC schedule was up to 2.2x less efficient at 50 ms than the Phase-3/4 MC because of large blocks; the cap removes that handicap from the MC comparator. This is a change made on Phase-5B data and applied here to new scenarios.
scheduler.fallback: if no RQMC schedule fits, the strategy falls back to MC and the method actually used is recorded; if MC does not fit either the run is infeasible

grid.note: 8 scenarios; none of these K/S0, sigma, T, r values occur in Phases 2-4 or in the other Phase-5 configs

loss: L = sum_g w_g MSE_g / s_g^2, s_g = per-path standard deviation of the plain-MC CPW-first estimator of Greek g (2^16 independent paths per scenario)

fixed_n.randomisation: Owen scrambling (as in Phase 4), reference-free: variance within training instance

strategies.shared-*: one simulation with the whole budget; all three Greeks from the same paths (MC, path PCA, or the equal-weight joint rotation, training amortised)
strategies.separate-*: three simulations with one third of the budget each (MC, path PCA, or each Greek's own rotation, training amortised)

break_even.model: total time M*B. A trained strategy simulates with B - C_train/M per valuation (C_train = median measured training time for that scenario; M = null means amortised, no charge); path PCA and MC simulate with B. GPCA-joint: one training, shared paths. GPCA-separate: three trainings, three simulations.
break_even.break_even: smallest M at which the geometric-mean loss ratio against shared path PCA is below 1 (point), and at which its 95% bootstrap upper bound is below 1 (significant)

transfer.base: first scenario of each m; rotation trained there (5 instances)
transfer.compare: path PCA; transferred rotation (trained on the base contract); fresh rotation (trained on the target contract, independent stream). Evaluation streams are independent of all training streams.
transfer.retraining_break_even: model-based only: a transferred rotation with loss ratio rho against a fresh one needs rho^(1/alpha) times the simulation time, so retraining pays after C_train / (B (rho^(1/alpha) - 1)) valuations

hypotheses.J1: Sharing paths: at equal total time the shared simulation has lower risk-vector loss than three separate simulations, for MC by about a factor 3 and for RQMC by more.
hypotheses.J2: The equal-weight joint rotation is within a factor 1.25 of the loss of rotations trained for other weightings, under every weighting (the rotation barely depends on the weights).
hypotheses.J3: Amortised, the joint rotation has lower loss than path PCA at equal time.
hypotheses.J4: Charged, there is a finite break-even M*; it is larger at small budgets and large m.
hypotheses.J5: A rotation transferred to a neighbouring contract stays better than path PCA and close to a freshly trained one; the loss grows with the distance in K, sigma or T.
